key_source: RE-CODING OF FIVE CELLS ONLY, 2026-09-07 (AP1, AP2, AP4, AP3, LR1), DE NOVO AND BLIND. The existing type row was withheld from the bundle; the fields below other than key_source are PLACEHOLDERS and MUST NOT overwrite the live row. WITNESS DEPENDENCE, MEASURED BEFORE ANY CELL WAS WRITTEN AND BINDING ON ALL FIVE. (1) TELEVANTOS 2020 AND GETZLER & MACNAIR 2005 ARE NOT INDEPENDENT. Counted across Televantos's full text: 'Getzler' 19 hits, 'Macnair' 10. Four are substantive citations of Getzler & Macnair 2005 - the introduction (n22, on asset partitioning as the book's frame), the partnership chapter's statement of the jingle rule (n51, citing 'Getzler and Macnair ... 267, 275-85'), the trusts chapter on bona fide purchase (n7), and the opening of the partnership-bankruptcy chapter (n2). The rest are the series editorship, the acknowledgements, an unrelated Macnair article, three citations of Getzler's own separate work, and bibliography and index entries. THE CRITICAL ONE IS THE JINGLE-RULE CITATION: Televantos cites Getzler & Macnair for the very rule AP1 turns on, so on AP1 they are one claim and its echo, not two witnesses. (2) BOTH SOURCES SIT INSIDE THE HANSMANN-KRAAKMAN(-SQUIRE) FRAMEWORK IN WHICH AP1 IS WORDED, so agreement between either of them and that framework is not corroboration of it. Getzler & Macnair cite Hansmann & Kraakman 2000. Televantos states the dependence himself: his book 'seeks to combine the insights of the law and economics theorists Hansmann and Kraakman' (printed 8, n22-23), and he glosses the jingle rule as "soft' entity shielding and asset partitioning, Hansmann, Kraakman, and Squire' (printed 146, n10). (3) GETZLER & MACNAIR ARE NOT INDEPENDENT OF HARRIS 2000, which is a coded source elsewhere in this census: they cite him four times and rely on him for the Bubble Act, for Eldon, and - decisively for this batch - for the assimilation of deed-of-settlement companies to partnership law (their n53, 'Deed of settlement companies were assimilated to partnership law, as is noted below. See further Harris, Industrializing English law'). They cite DuBois and Hunt only as orthodoxy to argue against. (4) TELEVANTOS'S ASSIMILATION CLAIM RESTS ON A WIDER BASE THAN THEIRS AND THIS IS A GAIN, NOT A DUPLICATION: he grounds it on DuBois 1938 quoted at length, on Gow's treatise of 1823, on Ker's Report on the Law of Partnership 1837, on Wordsworth 1845 and on Ireland, and he names Cooke 1950 as asserting the contrary without authority before 1852. (5) CITATION LIMIT ON GETZLER & MACNAIR: the copy in the bundle is the Oxford working-paper version, carries no folio marks, and no offset can be derived, SO NO CELL CITES A PRINTED PAGE FROM IT. Where it is cited at all it is cited by section heading and case name. (6) PAGE OFFSET FOR TELEVANTOS DERIVED IN THIS SESSION, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST: printed = PDF - 25, checked at eight points on both rectos and versos (PDF 41/printed 16, 42/17, 43/18, 101/76, 102/77, 151/126, 152/127, 201/176) and against the table of contents.
